test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 2 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 6 years more than 3 times the present age of the son. After 2 years, 2 times the father's age will be 7 years less than 5 times the son's age. The difference (in years) between the ages of the father and the son is:
solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the present age of the father be F years.

Let the present age of the son be S years.

F + S = 3S + 6

F = 3S - S + 6

F = 2S + 6 (Equation 1)

After 2 years:

Father's age will be F + 2 and Son's age will be S + 2

2 × (F + 2) = 5 × (S + 2) - 7

2F + 4 = 5S + 10 - 7

2F + 4 = 5S + 3

2F = 5S + 3 - 4

2F = 5S - 1 (Equation 2)

Substitute Equation 1 (F = 2S + 6) into Equation 2:

2 × (2S + 6) = 5S - 1

4S + 12 = 5S - 1

12 + 1 = 5S - 4S

13 = S

Now, substitute the value of S back into Equation 1:

F = 2S + 6

F = 2 × (13) + 6

F = 26 + 6 = 32

So, the father's present age (F) = 32 years.

Difference = Father's age - Son's age = 32 - 13 = 19 years

**∴ The difference between the ages of the father and the son is 19 years.**
